name: relics
layer_note: Church-held objects whose origin is debated. Not excavated finds.

properties.name: Shroud of Turin — Turin Cathedral (Chapel of the Holy Shroud)
properties.found: A linen cloth bearing the faint image of a crucified man, kept by the Catholic Church at Turin Cathedral. It is a church-held relic, not an excavated find.
properties.notes: John's 'linen cloths' (othonia) and the other Gospels' 'linen sheet' (sindon) can describe the same burial linens; 'strips' is one translation, not the only one (John 19:40; 20:5–7; Luke 24:12; Matthew 27:59; Mark 15:46; Luke 23:53). Some link the Shroud to the cloth 'folded in four' (tetradiplon) in the Acts of Thaddaeus (about 6th–7th century). This is one proposed reading, a modern hypothesis (Ian Wilson).
caveats: 1988 radiocarbon test: three labs dated samples to AD 1260–1390 (Damon et al., 1989).
Raw-data critique: a 2019 reanalysis of the 1988 raw data questions whether the samples were uniform (Casabianca et al., 2019).
2022 X-ray study: a wide-angle X-ray scattering study argued for a 1st-century date (De Caro et al., 2022), but it rests on one small sample and has not been independently repeated.
Even favorable reviewers separate 'an ancient burial cloth' from 'Jesus' own burial cloth'.
